title: Acting only on some passes
idea: MEET. Spotting when a loop should act only on SOME passes (if inside the loop) vs every pass. Thinking only.

exercises.prompt: 'Print each number 1 to 10, but only the even ones.' You act on...
options: only some passes — when the number is even
exercises.explanation: You print only on passes where the number is even, so an if inside the loop guards the action.

exercises.prompt: Which tool lets a loop act only on SOME passes?
options: an if inside the loop body
exercises.explanation: An if inside the loop checks a condition each pass and only acts when it is true.

exercises.prompt: 'Add up only the prices over 10' acts on some passes, not all.
exercises.explanation: True. You add only when the price is over 10, so an if inside the loop guards the accumulator.

exercises.prompt: Match each problem to 'every pass' or 'some passes'.
exercises.explanation: If a rule decides whether to act, it is 'some passes' (if inside the loop). No rule means every pass.

exercises.prompt: 'For each number 1 to 20, say Fizz if it divides by 3.' You act...
exercises.explanation: You check divisibility each pass and act only when it holds — an if inside the loop.

exercises.prompt: Skipping an action on some passes still means the loop runs every pass.
exercises.explanation: True. The loop visits every value; the if only decides whether to ACT. The pass still happens.

exercises.prompt: Order the plan for 'count the numbers 1 to 8 that are over 5'.
blocks: Inside, if the number is over 5, add 1 to the counter
After the loop, the counter is the answer
exercises.explanation: Visit every number, but only count the ones over 5 using an if inside the loop.

exercises.prompt: Which phrase signals 'act only on some passes'?
exercises.explanation: 'only the ones that ...' means a condition decides — an if inside the loop. The others mean every pass.

exercises.prompt: 'Print all 6 names, and star the ones starting with A.' How many actions happen?
options: Print happens every pass; the star only on some passes
Only the star, never the print
exercises.explanation: Printing is every pass; adding a star is guarded by an if (only names starting with A).

exercises.prompt: Why plan 'every pass vs some passes' before coding?
options: It tells you whether you need an if inside the loop
exercises.explanation: If only some passes act, you need an if inside the body. Spotting that shapes the plan.
